clue.text: Football body initially lambasts group defending top player's illegal move

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the next word is used
defending means one word wraps around and protects the other

parts.note: a set is a group of things
a top player is a star; the 's stands for 'has', joining to the definition

explanation.surface: A football authority criticises a squad shielding its star after a foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top player's' is the word that looks most like the definition's owner; the definition is just 'illegal move'.
explanation.definitionFit: A premature move before the signal in a race or game is a foul, so it is an illegal move.

clue.text: Be close to Bishop, fraternity

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a religious order is a fraternity of brothers

explanation.surface: Advice to stay near the bishop and the brotherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjoin or lie next to something is to touch its edge, hence to be close to it.

clue.text: Gallery employee maybe referring to shop by river

parts.note: re is a formal word meaning concerning or referring to
a store is a shop

explanation.surface: Someone who works in a gallery is described with reference to a riverside shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the river next to the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: An art gallery employs specialists who repair and clean damaged paintings; 'maybe' marks this as one example.

clue.text: Warbler talk

definitions.meaning: a stonechat or whinchat is a small songbird, known by a short name

explanation.surface: A songbird's chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a small songbird of the thrush family and an informal conversation share this short name.

clue.text: Form of gambling — son to cry over amount risked

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the next

parts.note: to weep is to cry
a stake is the sum wagered

explanation.surface: A gambler's son weeps over the money he has staked.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery-style bet in which all stakes are pooled and paid out to winners is a form of gambling.

clue.text: Country accountant overlooking nothing?

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooking means sitting above what follows

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
nada is Spanish-derived slang for nothing

explanation.surface: An accountant who fails to notice anything, in a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' reads as failing to notice but places CA above NADA.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American nation, the second largest by area in the world.

clue.text: One cleaning firm with almost all the fuel

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaner
CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: almost means the word all loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A cleaning company that takes nearly all the fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'the' are link words; 'almost' trims the last L from ALL to give AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbonised wood burnt in barbecues and braziers is a common solid fuel.

clue.text: God, angry, upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: sore means angry or aggrieved

explanation.surface: A deity who is cross and distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of love, son of Aphrodite, is a god.

clue.text: Better again, miles high?

definitions.meaning: recovered from illness; 'under the weather' means unwell, so its opposite means well again
literally higher than the clouds and storms, as a plane flies

explanation.surface: Someone recovered, or flying far up.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being restored to health, which taken literally describes flying above the clouds.

clue.text: Old president recalls a date selectively

indicators.note: selectively says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A former head of state remembers only some dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalls' looks like a reversal signal, but the run is read forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Anwar Sadat was Egypt's president from 1970 until his assassination in 1981.

clue.text: Reference work? That's bull, fellow's admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let inside, so one word takes the other in

parts.note: Taurus is the zodiac sign of the bull
a fellow is 'he', so fellow's is he's

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a reference work as nonsense, a bloke having confessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is a link word; 'bull' looks like slang for nonsense but is the star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of synonyms such as Roget's is consulted for words, a reference book.

clue.text: Shocks Spurs playing across slope

indicators.note: across means one set of letters stretches over the other, holding it inside
playing means the letters are put into play and rearranged

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur football club
a rise is an upward slope

explanation.surface: A football team stuns observers by playing on a sloping pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks like the team taking the field but signals the anagram, giving SURPS; 'across' means that jumble spans the slope word.
explanation.definitionFit: Unexpected events that startle people, as a synonym for jolts or shocks.

clue.text: Alert, calls for change in table feature?

indicators.note: for change asks for the letters to be altered into a different order

explanation.surface: A warning cry calls for something to be changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dish holding seasoning is set on a dining table, an item found there.

clue.text: Miss is enthusiastic about circular letter

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other

parts.note: avid means keen or enthusiastic
O is the letter shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A young woman is keen on a round-robin letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young woman but is the verb; 'circular letter' means a round letter, not a mailing.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer clear of or dodge something is to miss it.

clue.text: Seeing record making money — album's first to come out

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: to come out means that letter is removed

parts.note: earning means making money

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of album is taken

explanation.surface: Someone sees a record earning money, the album's first one to be released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come out' looks like a release date but drops A from EARNING, leaving ERNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Perceptive and showing good judgment; 'seeing' as an adjective means insightful.

clue.text: Rural aunt upset with lassie's game far away?

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of lassie are used; the 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition

explanation.surface: A country aunt is put out by a girl's game in a distant land.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses RURAL AUNT plus LASSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian football code played on oval fields, a sport from the far side of the world for British solvers.

clue.text: 4 or 9 say disheartened lady? Honestly?

parts.note: 4 and 9 are examples of numbers that are squares of whole numbers

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart of the word is removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Asking whether a woman's numbers are fair and if she is downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves L and Y of LADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Done fairly and directly, as in dealing above board, is acting honestly.

clue.text: Call right over publicity — find way round

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
an ad is an advertisement, publicity

explanation.surface: Phone the right person about advertising to find a route around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'find' is a link word; 'over' is not a positional signal but supplies O.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass circling a town lets traffic go around the centre, a road round it.

clue.text: The really upsetting sticky situation just starting — a bind

indicators.note: just starting means only the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A sticky predicament is beginning and leaves someone stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link word joining wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie up tightly, as a cook ties poultry, is to bind it.

clue.text: Decided one fancied at Wimbledon will welcome a learner

indicators.note: will welcome means taking the following letters inside

parts.note: a seed is a tennis player ranked as a favourite in a tournament such as Wimbledon
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A favourite at Wimbledon decides to welcome a novice player.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter that is settled or confirmed is sealed, as a deal is concluded.

clue.text: Way to get TV list included can be freshened up

indicators.note: included means placed inside the other word

parts.note: cable is one way television reaches homes
to list is to lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A cable TV listing that can be refreshed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' looks like a schedule but is the verb meaning tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that may be washed or tidied is able to be freshened up.

clue.text: Stop working after tease over low score

indicators.note: after means the first piece follows the second
over means the word is turned upside down, reading from the bottom up

parts.note: to rib is to tease
a machine that dies stops working

explanation.surface: Someone quits work after being mocked for a poor result.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, one under par on a hole is a good, low score.

clue.text: Fabric from Turin a pal ordered

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A friend in Turin places an order for cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterproofed heavy canvas used for covers is a sturdy fabric.

clue.text: Request time at first for work to be carried out

indicators.note: at first means this letter goes at the front

parts.note: to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Asking for time first so a job can be done.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of work or job assigned to someone to complete.

clue.text: Seize fastening device

definitions.meaning: to catch or arrest someone, informally
a metal spike hammered in to join pieces of wood

explanation.surface: Grab a fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for catching a culprit and a metal pin hammered into wood.

clue.text: Second showing somewhat poorer unfortunately

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A repeat broadcast is, sadly, a bit worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition was 'Second' alone, leaving 'showing' unused; the definition is 'Second showing', since a rerun is a repeat screening, not a second.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat broadcast of a programme already aired is its second screening.

clue.text: A fix, mental, is one turning to this?

definitions.text: A fix, mental, is one turning to this?

indicators.note: turning means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone in a mental fix turns to introspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to this' points to the answer: the whole clue describes someone in trouble looking inward.
explanation.definitionFit: Searching scrutiny of one's own conduct and motives is what a troubled mind may resort to.
